summary: JSON key casing (camelCase vs snake_case) causes idempotency mismatch for streaming function calls across SDKs
description:
Issue summary: Customers using the streaming function_call feature report intermittent duplicate downstream tool executions when using different SDKs (Python vs TS/Go). Root cause appears to be inconsistent JSON key casing for the idempotency token/metadata inside the function call payload which causes our dedup logic to miss matches.

Impact: Potential duplicate external side effects (webhook calls, job kicks) for customer workloads in dedicated clusters. Reported by multiple NovaHealth services; spikes observed during high-concurrency streaming sessions. Not full outage but high risk for billing and data correctness.

Environment: prod dedicated cluster (us-east), SDKs: py-sdk v1.8.3, ts-sdk v1.12.0, go-sdk v0.9.1. Streaming API over HTTP/2 and SSE clients observed. API gateway has an in-flight JSON key-normalization policy (legacy) enabled for some edge routes to try to canonicalize client payloads.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Use py-sdk to open a streaming chat session and include a function_call with metadata {"idempotency_key": "txn-ABC-123"}. 2) Use ts-sdk to open an equivalent streaming session but include metadata {"idempotencyKey": "txn-ABC-123"}. 3) Both clients call the same downstream webhook via a configured tool. 4) Observe server request logs: the webhook receives two executions for the same logical id because our function-call dedup logic did not see them as the same idempotency value.

Expected behavior: Function-call metadata idempotency token should be normalized/canonicalized server-side so different key casing still deduplicates to a single tool execution. SDKs should provide a clear guidance and (if possible) set the Idempotency header.

Actual behavior: Depending on the SDK and gateway route, key casing is preserved or translated inconsistently. The dedup engine looks for metadata.idempotency_key (snake_case) only; when the incoming JSON uses idempotencyKey (camelCase) or IdempotencyKey (PascalCase) the token is not observed and duplication occurs.

Relevant logs / examples:
- Raw capture (py-sdk): {"function_call": {"name": "start_job", "metadata": {"idempotency_key": "txn-ABC-123"}}}
- Raw capture (ts-sdk): {"function_call": {"name": "start_job", "metadata": {"idempotencyKey": "txn-ABC-123"}}}
- Dedup engine trace: WARN dedup: metadata.idempotency_key not found; fallback to header Idempotency-Key: null
- Webhook delivery log: delivered 2 events for txn-ABC-123 from stream session ids stream-99 and stream-101

Notes: Customers have relied on SDKs' example code which populates metadata with language-idiomatic keys (snake_case in Python examples, camelCase in TS). The API surface accepts free-form metadata JSON for function calls; previously dedup assumed snake_case. This is a regression introduced when the dedup engine was tightened to prefer a specific metadata path (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4100).

investigation_notes:
Hypothesis: Inconsistent JSON key casing combined with a dedup engine that only inspects a single metadata path results in missed matches. Evidence: request bodies from captured streams show different key spellings but same token value. The API gateway normalization is applied selectively by legacy route flag; TS examples produce camelCase, Python examples produce snake_case. Confirmed by checking SDK examples in repositories.

What we examined:
- Edge request bodies and raw HTTP/2 frames
- Dedup engine input logs and proto mapping
- Gateway JSON normalization rules (edge-config-v2)
- SDK example snippets in py-sdk and ts-sdk repos

Findings:
1) Dedup path hard-coded to metadata.idempotency_key.
2) Gateway sometimes converts keys to snake_case on ~30% of routes (legacy policy).
3) When gateway does not convert, TS clients send idempotencyKey which misses dedup.
4) No upstream header is set (Idempotency-Key) by SDKs in these code paths so header fallback is null.

Temporary mitigation tested:
- Add route-level gateway transform to copy any of the recognized keys into a canonical metadata.idempotency_key and set header Idempotency-Key. Tested in staging and small canary in prod us-east.
resolution_notes:
Short-term fix: Gateway transform rule applied to affected route in us-east to canonicalize idempotency keys and set Idempotency-Key header before dedup. This reduces surface area for duplicates immediately.

Medium-term fix: Update dedup engine to accept multiple canonical JSON paths and treat them equivalently (metadata.idempotency_key OR metadata.idempotencyKey OR metadata.IdempotencyKey) and continue to prefer header if present. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4582 (in review).

SDK guidance: Patch example code in py-sdk and ts-sdk to recommend setting the Idempotency header for cross-client workflows and to document that metadata keys might be normalized; SDK releases will include helper to set header automatically when metadata contains an idempotency token. PR in py-sdk: https://github.com/redwood-inference/py-sdk/pull/221 (merged).

Customer communication: NovaHealth notified; offered rollback and compensating job to reconcile duplicates. Finance engaged for billing adjustments.
workaround:
1) For immediate mitigation, customers should set the HTTP header 'Idempotency-Key' (or 'X-Idempotency-Key') with the token value in addition to placing it in function_call.metadata. This ensures server-side dedup path that prefers header will match.
2) If using edge routes configured with legacy normalization, request route update to enable canonicalization. Support can apply gateway transform for affected dedicated clusters on request.
follow_up_actions: Merge platform PR to accept multiple metadata key variants and add unit tests (owner: runtime-team, ETA: 2026-03-20).
Release sdk patches that set Idempotency header automatically when metadata contains an idempotency token (owners: sdk-team, ETA: py-sdk 1.8.4, ts-sdk 1.12.1).
Add telemetry and a rule to alert if duplicates > 0.1% for enterprise customers (owner: observability-team).
Update support runbook with guidance for idempotency header and JSON key normalization (owner: support-docs).
